terms.meaning: Mobile Application Security Verification Standard: 8 control groups, from STORAGE to PRIVACY.
Mobile Application Security Testing Guide: atomic tests, demos and best practices behind MASVS.
Mobile Application Security Weakness Enumeration: stable IDs for mobile weaknesses, grouped by MASVS.
OWASP's 2024 list of top mobile app risks, from M1 Improper Credential Usage to M10 Insufficient Cryptography.
Insecure Data Storage was M2 in the 2016 Mobile Top 10; the 2024 edition lists it as M9.
Essential Security profile: trusts OS controls; other apps on the device are the adversary.
Advanced Security profile: the OS can't be trusted; attackers may have physical access.
Resilient Security profile vs reverse engineering and tampering; the device user is the adversary.
MAS profile for EU Digital Identity Wallet instances; mapped to the EUDI Wallet risk register, (EU) 2024/2981.
MASVS v2.0.0 dropped per-control levels; L1, L2 and R now live as MAS Testing Profiles in the MASTG.
Control: The app securely stores sensitive data.
Control: The app performs identity pinning for all remote endpoints under the developer's control.
Control: The app validates the integrity of the platform.
Control: The app minimizes access to sensitive data and resources.
MASVS v1 pinning requirement ID and its MASVS v2 successor control (mapped via MASWE-0028).
App Vulnerable to Overlay Attacks (MASVS-PLATFORM); maps to CWE-1021.
Root/Jailbreak Detection Not Implemented (MASVS-RESILIENCE); applies to MAS-R.
Insertion of Sensitive Data into Logs was MASWE-0001 in the beta; MASWE v1.0.0 renumbered it 0005.
Deprecated v1 test 'Testing whether the App is Debuggable'; v2 covers it with 0226 (debuggable flag) and 0227.
Spreadsheet checklist removed as a release artifact in MASTG v2; the MAS website and repos are authoritative.
Mobile Security Testing Guide renamed Mobile Application Security Testing Guide in the 2022 OWASP MAS rebrand.
Platform key store that keeps key material out of the app process, optionally bound to TEE or StrongBox.
Keystore backed by an embedded secure element (Android 9+); attestation securityLevel 'StrongBox'.
Android 12 replaced the Keymaster HAL with the KeyMint HAL; the keystore daemon was rewritten in Rust.
Verified Boot state: locked, no custom root of trust. yellow = custom root of trust, orange = unlocked.
Mandatory access control mode where denials are logged and enforced; fully enforcing since Android 5.0.
Android XML config for trust anchors, pinning and cleartext policy, declared per app or per domain.
Network Security Config pin inside <pin-set>: base64 SHA-256 of a SubjectPublicKeyInfo.
NSC element: CT opt-in on Android 16 (API 36); on by default for apps targeting Android 17 (API 37).
Manifest flag planned for deprecation (Android 17 notice); cleartext rules move to Network Security Config.
Explicit export flag, mandatory for components with intent filters in apps targeting Android 12+.
Release-build manifest setting; a debuggable app is flagged by MASTG-TEST-0226.
Permission granted only to apps signed with the declaring app's cert; 'signatureOrSystem' deprecated in API 23.
Window flag marking content secure: kept out of screenshots and off non-secure displays.
FingerprintManager was deprecated in API 28; BiometricPrompt (API 28) provides the system biometric dialog.
Keystore key option (API 24) that invalidates a key when new biometrics are enrolled.
SafetyNet Attestation, deprecated in 2022, was turned down in Jan 2025; Play Integrity API replaces it.
Opt-in Play Integrity label: genuine certified device with recent security updates.

terms.text: v1 JAR signing → v2+ APK signing
terms.meaning: v1 signatures leave ZIP metadata unprotected; v2 (Android 7.0), v3 (9) and v3.1 (13) sign the whole APK.
Android 17 (API 37) hybrid APK signing: one classical signer plus one PQC signer (ML-DSA-65 or ML-DSA-87).
Full-disk encryption is not allowed on new devices with Android 10+; file-based encryption (Android 7.0+) replaces it.
Jetpack Security Crypto API, deprecated since 1.1.0-alpha07 (Apr 2025) in favor of platform APIs and Keystore.
Google Sign-In for Android is deprecated; Credential Manager unifies passkeys, passwords and federated sign-in.
Developer identity verification for apps on certified devices; first regional deadline Sep 30, 2026.
Digital Asset Links file that lets Android verify App Links (autoVerify) for a website.
Android isolates each app under its own Linux UID, with SELinux and seccomp adding layers.
iOS encrypted store for small secrets such as passwords and keys, with per-item accessibility classes.
Dedicated secure subsystem in Apple SoCs that isolates keys and biometric data from the main processor.
iOS networking policy requiring secure HTTPS connections by default; configured under NSAppTransportSecurity.
Info.plist Boolean that disables ATS restrictions for all network connections (iOS 9+).
ATS key (iOS 14+) declaring the public-key identities expected for named domains.
Data Protection Class A: file unreadable while the device is locked; key tied to passcode and device UID.
Keychain accessibility deprecated in iOS 12; Apple suggests kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock instead.
DeviceCheck service (iOS 14+) that lets a server validate the app instance running on a device.
Privacy manifest: collected data, tracking domains, required reason APIs (reasons required since May 1, 2024).
Debug entitlement; if enabled in a release build it is flagged by MASTG-TEST-0261.
UIWebView was deprecated in iOS 12; Apple's documentation says to use WKWebView instead.
Optional extreme protection (iOS 16+): blocks most message attachments and certain complex web technologies.
Messages and IDS mitigation (iOS 14+) using sandbox restrictions and memory-safe validation.
On A15+/M2+ chips, Secure Page Table Monitor with TXM replaces the Page Protection Layer.
Always-on memory safety built on EMTE in all iPhone 17 and iPhone Air models (announced Sep 2025).
Signature proving an app's origin and integrity; iOS runs only code signed with an Apple-issued certificate.
2015 Android media library (libstagefright) bug family; this integer overflow is one of its CVEs.
2016 chain of three iOS zero-days (WebKit + kernel) used by Pegasus spyware; fixed in iOS 9.3.5.
2021 zero-click iMessage exploit; CoreGraphics integer overflow via crafted PDF, fixed in iOS 14.8.
2023 zero-click iOS spyware chain; CVE-2023-38606 let an app modify sensitive kernel state.
Public exploit for a 2019 SecureROM (bootrom) use-after-free in Apple A5-A11; needs physical access, DFU mode.
2017 Android flaw hitting APKs signed only with v1 JAR signing; v2 signatures are not affected.
2020 Android task-hijacking flaw: confused deputy in startActivities, a local privilege escalation.
Dynamic instrumentation toolkit; the workhorse of runtime mobile app testing.
Runtime mobile exploration toolkit built on Frida.
Mobile Security Framework: automated static and dynamic analysis for Android and iOS apps.
Dex-to-Java decompiler for reading Android app code.
Decodes APK resources and smali and rebuilds packages.
Systemless root suite for Android, widely used to root test devices.
Android security assessment framework for probing app IPC surfaces.
Virtualized Arm devices (iOS and Android) used for mobile security research and testing.
OWASP MAS Android crackme, level 1 of the UnCrackable reverse-engineering challenges.
Trusting only pre-defined server certs or keys; MASVS calls it identity pinning.
Modern iOS jailbreak style that leaves the sealed system volume untouched; files live under /var/jb.
Installing apps from outside the official app store.
Unpacking, modifying and re-signing an app; countered by anti-tampering and attestation.
Runtime Application Self-Protection: in-app signals that detect a hostile environment and react.
Overlay attack where a malicious window hides the real UI to capture the user's taps.
NIST 'Vetting the Security of Mobile Applications' (April 2019).
OAuth 2.0 for Native Apps (Oct 2017, Best Current Practice): external user-agents, not embedded ones.
Improper Export of Android Application Components.
App Defense Alliance Mobile Application Security Assessment, a certification built on OWASP MASVS.
CISA mobile guidance, general recommendation 5: add a carrier account PIN so that number porting and SIM swaps need it.
CISA mobile guidance, first iPhone tip: turn on Lockdown Mode to shrink the attack surface of highly targeted people.
The point of Keystore and Secure Enclave: keys are used, never exported.

spec.as: A key that never leaves the chip cannot be copied off it.

terms.meaning: Certificate pinning narrows trust from any CA to the expected key.

spec.as: Pin the server key, do not trust every certificate authority.

terms.meaning: Android gives every app its own UID; iOS confines apps to a container.

spec.as: Each app runs as its own user, so a bug stays in its box.

terms.meaning: KeyProperties.SECURITY_LEVEL_UNKNOWN = -2: no statement can be made about where a key lives.
KeyProperties.SECURITY_LEVEL_UNKNOWN_SECURE = -1: at least as strong as a TEE, exact level unknown.
Latin a and Cyrillic а, the classic lookalike in fake package names.
Latin o and Cyrillic о.
Latin p and Cyrillic р.
Latin x and Cyrillic х.
Known-answer test: the RFC's published SHA-1 test key at Unix time 59 gives 94287082.
Known-answer test: the RFC's published SHA-1 test key at counter 0 gives 755224.
Known-answer test: One iteration of PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 over "password" and "salt", 20 bytes.

terms.text: Pin digest of the empty string
terms.meaning: Known-answer test: Base64 of SHA-256 of zero bytes, the value pin-set examples start from.
Disabling iOS protections, code signing above all, so unsigned code can run; Apple calls it unauthorized modification.
Modifying Android so commands can run as the root user, bypassing restrictions such as app sandboxing.
Isolated area of the main processor that protects sensitive code and data from the rich OS around it.
Commercial spyware linked to NSO Group; ATT&CK tracks it as S0289 for iOS and S0316 for Android.
Android Debug Bridge: command-line tool that talks to a device or emulator for app install, debugging and shell.
Built-in Android malware defense from Google that scans apps and warns about or blocks harmful ones.
Android model (6.0+) where the user grants dangerous permissions while the app runs, not at install time.
Chain of trust from a hardware root through the bootloader to verified partitions, with rollback protection.
Apple-signed file tying together who may sign an app, where it can run and which entitlements it may use.
Key-value pairs embedded in an app's code signature that grant it a right to use a service or technology.
